title: Berka Czech bank, 1993-1998
origin: PKDD 1999 financial dataset by Petr Berka, published again in BIRD and in FINCH.
why_this_file: The column names A2 and A11 do not say what they mean. A production text-to-SQL system keeps this dictionary beside the database. The model reads the dictionary, not a guess.

district.purpose: 77 Czech districts. Demographics for 1995 and 1996. One row per district.

columns.district_id: Primary key. Branch and client tables point here.
columns.A2: District name, for example Pisek or Hl.m. Praha.
columns.A3: Region name, for example east Bohemia or Prague.
columns.A4: Number of inhabitants. Stored as text in this file.

account.purpose: One row per bank account. 4500 accounts, opened from 1993 to 1997.

columns.district_id: District of the branch that opened the account. Joins to district.district_id.
columns.frequency: How often the bank prints a statement. Use the stored Czech code, not the English word.
columns.date: Date the account was opened. Format YYYY-MM-DD.

client.purpose: One row per client. Gender and birth date were decoded from the original birth number.

columns.district_id: District where the client lives. Joins to district.district_id.

disp.purpose: Links a client to an account. This is the bridge between people, accounts, cards, and loans.

type.OWNER: the account owner, the person who can be granted a loan
type.DISPONENT: a person allowed to operate the account who is not the owner

card.purpose: Credit cards. 892 cards. The type is stored in lowercase.

columns.disp_id: Joins to disp.disp_id. A card belongs to a disposition, not directly to a client.
columns.type: Credit card type, stored in lowercase: classic, gold, or junior.
columns.issued: Date the card was issued, YYYY-MM-DD.

loan.purpose: 682 loans. Amount is in Czech crowns.

columns.date: Date the loan was approved, YYYY-MM-DD.
columns.duration: Length of the loan in months.
columns.status: One letter: A, B, C, or D.

order.purpose: Standing orders. The table name is a SQL reserved word, so it must be written as "order".

columns.k_symbol: Purpose code. A blank means the purpose was not filled in.

trans.purpose: 1,056,320 transactions from 1993 through 1998. Filter this table. Do not read it without a WHERE.

columns.date: Transaction date, YYYY-MM-DD. Use strftime('%Y', date) for the four-digit calendar value. The code %y returns two digits.
columns.type: Direction of the money: PRIJEM, VYDAJ, or VYBER.
columns.operation: How the money moved. More precise than type.
columns.k_symbol: Purpose of the transaction. Empty when the bank did not record one.
columns.bank: Partner bank code, for example AB or QR.

type.VYBER: cash withdrawal recorded in the type column

k_symbol.SANKC. UROK: sanction interest on a negative balance
